get.summary: What the codes of the answers mean: idtrack's own tables, the api's where idtrack has none
get.description: What every code in an answer means: idtrack's own tables (statuses, reasons, step reasons, criteria, match steps and prefixes, reading reasons, place relations, bridge rules, the fields of a candidate) and, where idtrack has none, the api's own words (marked by `source`), and the api's error codes. Read it once and keep it (`ETag`).

statuses.meaning: One best answer: the identifier leads to one target in the requested database.
Several genes or targets are equal in all the evidence that decides; all of them are the best answer, in ascending order of gene id and target id.

reasons.meaning: The identifier is not an identifier of this graph at any release.
The identifier is an Ensembl id, or a sequence accession, with a version this graph does not hold.

step_reasons.meaning: The gene exists at the target release.
The identifier is attached to this gene at the release it is read at.

criteria.meaning: The gene is the queried gene id's own version at the target release (an id that exists at the target release is its own answer).

0: the target is attached to the gene at the target release; 1: attached to a transcript or translation that belonged to the gene at another release; `null`: no gene has an id in the requested database and the gene itself is the target.

candidate_fields.meaning: The Ensembl gene (`<id>.<version>`) at the target release through which the target was reached.
The id in the final database, as that database wrote it at the target release (the gene itself for `ensembl_gene`).

match_steps.meaning: The identifier as written (for an external identifier: as a database wrote it at the release read).
The identifier when letter case is ignored.

match_prefixes.meaning: In a batch: a name made unique by a single-cell tool (another item of the batch with -1, .1 or _1 appended, itself no exact name at the release it is read at alone); the result is that item's.

Unicode was normalised before matching: invisible and control characters (zero-width characters, byte-order marks, bidirectional marks, soft hyphens) removed, compatibility forms (NFKC: full-width letters and digits) and Unicode dashes read as their plain characters.

reading_reasons.meaning: In an organism whose symbols follow a letter-case convention, a string written otherwise that is not exactly a name is read first as a symbol of the organism without letter case, where that names exactly one gene; this reading came after it.

The string ends in a suffix that single-cell tools append to make names unique (-1, .1, _1); reading it, with its separators taken as one or without letter case, as a synonym of another gene than the string before the suffix names is not taken.

place_relations.meaning: On one assembly the two genes overlap (one sequence region, one strand), or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies overlaps it.

On one assembly the two genes do not overlap: another sequence region, another strand, or apart; or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies shares no base with it; or a copy's reference region (Ensembl's assembly exception) shares no base with the other gene; or, on two assemblies that no published mapping joins, they lie on chromosomes of different names (the mitochondrial genome against a chromosome among them), which no assembly change turns one into the other.

bridge_rules.meaning: Taken: the two genes overlap on one assembly, or Ensembl's mapping of their two assemblies carries one onto the other.
Taken: the places of the two genes cannot be compared (two assemblies, a sequence of one name or a scaffold), and no release gives the id to both: the id left one gene for the other.

errors.title: The request is not in the form the endpoint takes.
errors.meaning: The request does not have the shape the endpoint takes: a missing or malformed parameter, a body that is not UTF-8 JSON of the documented shape (`details` lists each problem, `argument` names the parameter when one is at fault).

errors.title: The request names a parameter the endpoint does not take, or names one twice.
errors.meaning: A query parameter the endpoint does not take, or one given more than once.

database_kinds.meaning: One of idtrack's two Ensembl gene namespaces: `ensembl_gene`, the gene id with its version, and `base_ensembl_gene`, without (`versioned` says which).
An external database whose ids are accessions (NCBI's gene numbers in `EntrezGene`, RefSeq's and UniProt's accessions); where the graph holds its labels apart, `labels` names their database.

allowances.meaning: Searching requests (`rate_per_minute` per minute, `rate_burst` at once).
Every other request of the api (`read_share` times the searches' allowance).

source_modes.meaning: An origin is a release (counted only on the assembly that serves it).

cautions.meaning: The best answer is reached through a bridge: where Ensembl's history gives a gene no successor, the walk left it through an id it carries and entered another gene that carries the same id. That is idtrack's inference; no record of Ensembl states it.

A bridge on the best answer's path joins two genes that lived at the same releases: the gene it enters did not take the place of the gene it leaves in Ensembl's records, so their shared ids are no sign of succession.

get.summary: Convert one identifier: every candidate ranked, the best marked, optionally its path
get.description: Convert one identifier (idtrack's `API.convert`): how the string was read, every candidate the search reached, ranked, the best marked, the criterion that decided between the best and the runner-up, the reason of a result without answer, and with `explain=true` the path of every candidate as a graph of nodes and steps. An identifier not in the graph is not an error: it is a result with status `not_found`. Only `converted` and `tie` answer in the requested database: for `no_target`, `final_database` is `ensembl_gene` and the best candidates are the genes reached, standing in for the missing id.

parameters.description: The organism: its Ensembl production name (`homo_sapiens`), with spaces or in any letter case (`Homo sapiens`), or a short name idtrack declares (`human`, `pig`); the names a server holds: `names` of `GET /organisms`.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: An Ensembl id (with or without version), a symbol or another id of a database the graph holds (`external_databases` of `GET /organisms/{organism}`). White space at its ends is no part of it. Ids of databases the graph does not hold are `not_found`: the name authorities' own ids (`HGNC:11998`), UniProt's secondary accessions, entry names and isoforms, RNAcentral, microarray probe sets (`201746_at`).

parameters.name: from_release
parameters.description: The release it is read at; omitted: inferred. Without it, an identifier is read at the target release if it exists there, and otherwise at the latest release at which it exists (idtrack's rule, the same for Ensembl ids, symbols and other databases' ids); the result says which release was used (`from_release`) and whether it was chosen (`from_release_inferred`). So a symbol sent without `from_release` is read as what it names at the target release, not as what it named years ago: give the release of the list's source to read it as it was then (`POST .../source-inference` finds it for a list). An Ensembl release, a whole number from 0 to 999999999 (anything else is `400 invalid_request`); whether the graph covers it is idtrack's to answer (`400 unknown_release`, with the graph's releases in `allowed`: `GET /organisms/{organism}` lists them as `releases`).

parameters.name: to_release
parameters.description: The target release; omitted: the snapshot release. An Ensembl release, a whole number from 0 to 999999999 (anything else is `400 invalid_request`); whether the graph covers it is idtrack's to answer (`400 unknown_release`, with the graph's releases in `allowed`: `GET /organisms/{organism}` lists them as `releases`).

parameters.name: final_database
parameters.description: The database of the targets; omitted: `ensembl_gene`. The values a release takes: `GET /organisms/{organism}/final-databases?to_release=`; what each holds: `kind` of `GET /organisms/{organism}/databases` (NCBI's gene numbers are `EntrezGene`, its symbols `NCBI gene (formerly Entrezgene)`).

parameters.name: from_database
parameters.description: The database the identifier is meant in; omitted: any. The values: `external_databases` of `GET /organisms/{organism}` (a database's synonyms are read under its name). An identifier that is not an id of the database named is read as absent from it (`no_conversion` with `no_gene_at_start`, or `not_found`), not as retired; some databases come in two forms, accessions and their labels (`RefSeq_peptide` and `RefSeq peptide`: `kind` of `GET /organisms/{organism}/databases`).

parameters.description: Add the path of every candidate (`path`); it makes answers much larger. Written true or false.

post.summary: Convert a batch with the same arguments; results in input order, each with its own status
post.description: Convert many identifiers at once (idtrack's `API.convert_many`): one result per identifier in input order, each with its own status. An identifier whose conversion fails is that item's `status: "error"` with `error.code`, and the batch goes on; an identifier the api refuses at its boundary (too long, control characters inside it) refuses the whole batch (`400 invalid_identifier`, every such index in `details`). With `read_copies` (the default) an item can be answered as the copy of another item of the same batch. `format=tsv` gives one row per candidate. Prefer it to many single calls.

schema.description:
A table of tab-separated values, UTF-8, each line ending in a line feed: the first line names the columns, then one row per candidate of each result in input order (a result without candidates: one row, its candidate columns empty). A result's columns repeat on each of its rows. Each value as the JSON answer writes it: `null` as an empty cell; `true` and `false` as those words; a number as written in the JSON answer (nothing rounded); a list's items joined by `;`. The explained path (`path`, `final_path`) is not in the table: ask for JSON. With `provenance=true`, one line before the header begins with `#` and names the graph and the request (`Content-Disposition` names the file after the organism, the target release and the graph's digest). The columns, in order (also as `x-columns`):

| Column | Of | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input_index` | result | The item's place in the batch, from 0 (the result's place in `results`). |
| `query_id` | result | `query_id`: the identifier as sent (escaped: a backslash before `\`, `t`, `n`, `r`). |
| `status` | result | `status` of the result. |
| `reason` | result | `reason` of the result. |
| `reasons` | result | `reasons` of the result. |
| `graph_id` | result | `graph_id` of the result. |
| `match` | result | `match` of the result. |
| `known_versions` | result | `known_versions` of the result. |
| `from_release` | result | `from_release` of the result. |
| `from_release_inferred` | result | `from_release_inferred` of the result. |
| `from_release_given` | result | `from_release_given` of the result. |
| `from_release_fallback` | result | `from_release_fallback` of the result. |
| `from_databases` | result | `from_databases` of the result. |
| `to_release` | result | `to_release` of the result. |
| `final_database` | result | `final_database` of the result. |
| `candidate_count` | result | The number of the result's candidates (its rows; 0 on the one row of a result without any). |

x-enum-descriptions: On one assembly the two genes overlap (one sequence region, one strand), or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies overlaps it.

On one assembly the two genes do not overlap: another sequence region, another strand, or apart; or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies shares no base with it; or a copy's reference region (Ensembl's assembly exception) shares no base with the other gene; or, on two assemblies that no published mapping joins, they lie on chromosomes of different names (the mitochondrial genome against a chromosome among them), which no assembly change turns one into the other.
The two genes never lie on one assembly at the same time, and nothing tells them apart (a sequence of one name, or a scaffold): their places cannot be compared.

A gene lies outside the reference sequence (a patch, a haplotype, an alternative locus, an LRG record), and nothing places it apart from the other gene (it lies inside its assembly exception's reference region, or it is an LRG record, which has none): its place is not compared base by base with the reference sequence.

Refused: a synonym is no bridge (it names other genes too often to stand for one).

The best answer descends through a split of Ensembl's history, and other successors were reached: IDTrack ranks the successors of a split by Ensembl's scores and the candidates' evidence, not by which of them lies where the old gene lay.
The same string is also read as another id at the same step.
The identifier's version was not judged (`version_not_judged`).
The identifier was read after a Unicode normalisation.
The identifier was read with punctuation removed.
A gene's copy on the Y chromosome's pseudoautosomal region was read as its gene.
An LRG record was read as its gene.
The lowest of Ensembl's mapping scores on the best answer's path, stated exactly (the candidate's score is the product of the scores along its path).

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: What it means, in the api's words.

reads_path.title: Reads Path
reads_path.description: Whether its rule reads the path (its steps, nodes or bridges).

limitation.title: Limitation
limitation.description: The address of the section of idtrack's documented limitations of this class, if any.

CautionTerm.title: CautionTerm
CautionTerm.description: A class of evidence of the cautions, its tone and meaning, and the limitation it falls under.

graph_id.title: Graph Id
graph_id.description: The identifier of the graph the identifier was read as (`null`: not found). For an Ensembl transcript or translation id without version this is its version of the starting release. A synonym is written as it is (`match` says it is a synonym).

x-match-prefixes.copy: In a batch: a name made unique by a single-cell tool (another item of the batch with -1, .1 or _1 appended, itself no exact name at the release it is read at alone); the result is that item's.
x-match-prefixes.unicode: Unicode was normalised before matching: invisible and control characters (zero-width characters, byte-order marks, bidirectional marks, soft hyphens) removed, compatibility forms (NFKC: full-width letters and digits) and Unicode dashes read as their plain characters.
x-match-prefixes.punctuation: Stray punctuation was removed before matching: quotes around the identifier, and the punctuation that ends a sentence, a clause or an item of a list at its end (a semicolon, comma, full stop, colon, exclamation or question mark).
x-match-prefixes.par_y: GENCODE's form of the Y copy of a pseudoautosomal gene (<id>_PAR_Y) was read as the gene's id; the Y copy is reported apart.
x-match-prefixes.lrg: An LRG record's id, answered with the gene the record describes.
x-match-prefixes.synonym: A synonym that a database records for the gene, not the name the database gives it.

x-match-steps.exact: The identifier as written (for an external identifier: as a database wrote it at the release read).
x-match-steps.case: The identifier when letter case is ignored.
x-match-steps.separator: The identifier when '-', '_' and '.' are taken as one character (and letter case is ignored).
x-match-steps.version: A sequence accession with the version written after it, read where Ensembl's cross references attached that version.
x-match-steps.version_newer_than_graph: An Ensembl id or a sequence accession with a version newer than every version the graph holds, read as its latest version (an id active, an accession attached, at the graph's last release).
x-match-steps.version_not_judged: A sequence accession with a version that is not judged: Ensembl's records hold only an edit counter of the records of its database (UniProt's entry version), so the accession is read without it.

match.title: Match
match.description: How the identifier matched `graph_id`: a step of `match_steps` of `GET /vocabulary` after the prefixes of `match_prefixes` of `GET /vocabulary` that apply (`"synonym:exact"`, `"unicode:case"`); `null` when it is not in the graph.

known_versions.title: Known Versions
known_versions.description: For an Ensembl id, or a sequence accession, written with a version the graph does not hold: the versions that exist (the identifier is not answered with another version's gene).

from_release.title: From Release
from_release.description: The release at which the identifier was read.

from_release_inferred.title: From Release Inferred
from_release_inferred.description: The release was chosen by the engine, not given.

from_release_fallback.title: From Release Fallback
from_release_fallback.description: The release given was set aside because the graph does not hold the identifier there; it was read where the graph holds it.

from_databases.title: From Databases
from_databases.description: For an external id, the databases through which it was read at that release (for a synonym: the databases that record it).

final_database.title: Final Database
final_database.description: The database of the targets: the requested one, `ensembl_gene` when the genes reached have no id in it (`no_target`), `null` when nothing was found.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: Every target reached, ranked, the best first and marked.

tie.title: Tie
tie.description: The best answer is shared by several genes or targets equal in all evidence.

x-enum-descriptions: The criterion `own_version` decided.
The criterion `final_confidence` decided.
The criterion `bridges` decided.
The criterion `bridge_gap` decided.
The criterion `display_name` decided.
The criterion `entry_support` decided.
The criterion `score` decided.

The criterion `annotation` decided.

decided_by.title: Decided By
decided_by.description: The criterion (`criteria` of `GET /vocabulary`) that put the best answer before the runner-up; `null` without a runner-up.

alternative_locus_genes.title: Alternative Locus Genes
alternative_locus_genes.description: Copies on alternative loci and patches, LRG records, and the Y copies of pseudoautosomal genes (beside their gene on X), that the identifier also leads to beside genes of the reference sequence; not candidates.

no_target.title: No Target
no_target.description: Genes were reached, but none has an id in the requested database; the candidates are the genes.

no_target_genes.title: No Target Genes
no_target_genes.description: Genes reached without an id in the requested database while others have one; not candidates.

status.title: Status
x-enum-descriptions: One best answer: the identifier leads to one target in the requested database.

Genes were reached at the target release, but none of the genes of the best answer has an id in the requested database: the candidates are the genes themselves, never another gene's id.
The identifier is not in the graph: unknown, or of a database the graph does not include.
An Ensembl id or a sequence accession with a version the graph does not hold; the versions that exist are listed (`known_versions`), and no other version's gene is answered.
The identifier is in the graph, but no gene at the target release descends from it (a retired id, for instance); `reasons` says why.
In a batch: the conversion of this identifier raised an error (`error`); the batch went on.
The identifier is not an identifier of this graph at any release.
The identifier is an Ensembl id, or a sequence accession, with a version this graph does not hold.
The version written after the accession was not judged: Ensembl's records hold only an edit counter of the records of its database, not a version of the sequence; the accession was read without it.
The identifier is an Ensembl id, not an id of the database named as its source.
The identifier is never active on the assemblies that serve the releases of this graph.
At the release it is read at, the identifier is attached to no gene.
Ensembl's history (and the bridges allowed) leads to no gene at the target release.
The genes reached have no id in the requested database.
The conversion of this identifier raised an error (see `error`).

The graph does not hold the identifier at the release given (`from_release_given`); it was read where the graph holds it (`from_release`), so the targets are what the identifier meant there, which can be another gene than the one it meant at the release given.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: The first of `reasons`; `null` when none applies.

x-enum-descriptions: The identifier is not an identifier of this graph at any release.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: Every reason that applies, keys of `reasons` of `GET /vocabulary`, in this order: why the result has no target in the requested database (no candidates, or `no_target`: genes stand in for the missing id); `"read_at_another_release"` where the identifier was read at another release than the one given (`from_release_fallback`); `"version_not_judged"` where a version written after an accession was not judged (its database's versions count edits of the record and do not date it). Empty for a result with targets read as asked.

other_readings.title: Other Readings
other_readings.description: The other nodes the identifier was read as: those a rule of name resolution put after `graph_id`, with what they would answer, those read by the same step, whose candidates are part of a tie, and those the string has at other releases only, with those releases (`idtrack.graph.TheGraph.readings`).

error.description: In a batch, the error that stopped this identifier's conversion.

path.description: With `explain`: the paths of the candidates (no step when there is no candidate) and the bridges the search considered; `null` without `explain`.

cautions.title: Cautions
cautions.description: The api's reading of this result's evidence, by stated rules (`cautions` of `GET /vocabulary`): each fact of the best answer a reader should weigh before trusting it (`tone` `caution`: review the answer) or that is worth knowing (`note`), cautions first, with the section of idtrack's documented limitations it falls under. Read with the path whatever `explain` asks: every rule holds for every answer. Empty: nothing to weigh. Added by the api to idtrack's result.

ConversionResult.title: ConversionResult
ConversionResult.description: One identifier converted to a target release and database (`idtrack.API.convert`).

cores_used.title: Cores Used
cores_used.description: The sum of `cpu_share` over the master and the workers: cores kept busy over the last interval. `null` when a process's share is unknown.

share_of_available.title: Share Of Available
share_of_available.description: `cores_used` over `cores_available`: `1.0` is every available core busy.

cores_available.title: Cores Available
cores_available.description: The cores the server may use: the smaller of `affinity_cores` and `quota_cores`.

affinity_cores.title: Affinity Cores
affinity_cores.description: The CPUs the processes may run on (their CPU affinity set; off Linux, the machine's CPU count).

quota_cores.title: Quota Cores
quota_cores.description: A cgroup v2 `cpu.max` quota in cores (quota over period), the smallest of the server's cgroup and its ancestors (a container's limit); `null` when none is set.

source.title: Source
source.description: What sets `cores_available`: the cgroup quota, the affinity set, or the machine's CPU count.

CpuLoad.title: CpuLoad
CpuLoad.description: The server's CPU use against the cores available to it.

first.title: First
first.description: Which value ranks first: `yes` (true before false), `lower` or `higher` (a tuple compared part by part, from its first part).

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: For a field that is a tuple, the names of its parts, each the negated count (as idtrack's text of the field states); `null` otherwise.

CriterionField.title: CriterionField
CriterionField.description: A `Candidate` field a criterion compares, and which of its values ranks first.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: idtrack's text of the `Candidate` field of the same name.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The fields idtrack's ranking compares for this criterion, in order, the first that differs deciding (the api's reading of idtrack's ranking, which gives no such table; tested against idtrack's criteria).

CriterionTerm.description: A criterion that ranks candidates: idtrack's text of its field, and the fields its ranking compares.

result.description: The result, exactly as `GET .../convert` answers it with this `final_database` (and without `explain`): for `no_target` its `final_database` is `ensembl_gene`, so `database` keeps the one asked for.

DatabaseConversion.title: DatabaseConversion
DatabaseConversion.description: One identifier converted into one database.

form.title: Form
form.description: The Ensembl form the database connects through (`gene`, `transcript`, `translation`: idtrack's `API.database_forms()`); `null` for idtrack's own gene namespaces `ensembl_gene` and `base_ensembl_gene`, which that table does not list.

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: The releases whose `final_databases` include it (idtrack's `API.final_databases(to_release)`), ascending.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What its values are (`database_kinds` of `GET /vocabulary`): `ensembl`, one of idtrack's two Ensembl gene namespaces; `label`, a database whose ids are labels (display names, symbols) rather than accessions (the graph's `label_databases`); `accession`, any other external database.

versioned.title: Versioned
versioned.description: For `ensembl`: whether its values carry the Ensembl version (`ensembl_gene`: `ENSG00000141510.20`; `base_ensembl_gene`: `ENSG00000141510`); `null` for an external database.

authority.title: Authority
authority.description: Whether it is a database of a name authority of the organism (the graph's `authority_databases`: its symbol databases and NCBI's official symbols).

labels.title: Labels
labels.description: For an `accession` database whose labels the graph holds apart: the database of its labels (the graph's `label_names`: `EntrezGene`, NCBI's gene numbers, has its official symbols in `NCBI gene (formerly Entrezgene)`); `null` otherwise.

labels_of.title: Labels Of
labels_of.description: For a `label` database: the accession databases whose labels it holds (empty for none, or another kind).

former_names.title: Former Names
former_names.description: Names Ensembl gave the database at some release that the graph does not use (the graph's `renamed_databases`): sent as `final_database` or `from_database`, such a name is refused with the graph's name in the message.

DatabaseReleases.title: DatabaseReleases
DatabaseReleases.description: An external database (or one of Ensembl's gene namespaces) and the releases a conversion can end in it.

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: Every release of the graph, ascending: the matrix's columns.

databases.title: Databases
databases.description: Every database a conversion to some release can end in, sorted by name: the matrix's rows. The cell of a release and a database is set when the release is in the database's `releases`.

by_assembly.title: By Assembly
by_assembly.description: The external databases of each genome assembly of the graph (idtrack's `API.databases_by_assembly()`; an assembly by its number, as a string). A release's databases are those of the assembly that serves it (`assemblies[].serves` of `/organisms/{organism}`) and the two gene namespaces.

symbol_databases.title: Symbol Databases
symbol_databases.description: The organism's symbol databases, its name authorities, in idtrack's order (`idtrack.organisms.SYMBOL_DATABASES`): the first one a conversion to a release can end in is the one idtrack's harmonization uses by default there.

DatabasesResponse.title: DatabasesResponse
DatabasesResponse.description: What a conversion to each release of a graph can end in: a release-by-database matrix, and per assembly.

to_release.title: To Release
to_release.description: `to_release` of the query (the one used: `to_release` above).

EachDatabaseArguments.title: EachDatabaseArguments
EachDatabaseArguments.description: The arguments of `convert/each-database` as the api read them (`null`: not given, the default applies).

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.description: One conversion per database of `GET .../final-databases?to_release=`, in that order (`ensembl_gene` among them).

EachDatabaseResponse.title: EachDatabaseResponse
EachDatabaseResponse.description: One identifier converted into every database a conversion to the target release can end in.

code.title: Code
code.description: A stable code of the kind of error: branch on it (its meaning, title and whether to retry: `errors` of `GET /api/v1/vocabulary`).
x-enum-descriptions: The request does not have the shape the endpoint takes: a missing or malformed parameter, a body that is not UTF-8 JSON of the documented shape (`details` lists each problem, `argument` names the parameter when one is at fault).
A query parameter the endpoint does not take, or one given more than once.

An identifier or name is longer than this server accepts, or holds control, surrogate, private-use or unassigned characters (in a batch: the whole batch is refused, and `details` gives every such item's index).
A release the graph does not cover (`allowed` lists the graph's releases).
A database the graph does not hold at that release (`allowed` lists those it holds).
An identifier the call needs to exist in the graph does not (the gene of names-of).
An identifier is empty or a spelling of a missing value (IDTrack's refusal), or a name to look up is empty.
An argument whose value is not accepted (an empty or over-long database name).
Another input IDTrack refuses (IDTrack's message says which).
An organism this server does not hold (`allowed` lists those it holds).
No such endpoint or file.
The endpoint does not take this method (the `Allow` header and `allowed` list the methods it takes).
The request's head or body did not arrive within the time the server waits for it, or its client closed the connection before its search (which is then not run); send it again.
The request body is larger than the server accepts.
A batch with more identifiers than the server accepts (`batch_max` of /limits).
The request's path and query are longer than the server accepts.
A request body that is not `application/json` in UTF-8, or that is sent compressed (`Content-Encoding`).
One identifier's search needed more than its budget (states or seconds); the same request fails again.

This client sent more requests, or used more search time, than its allowance; wait the `Retry-After` header's seconds.
A fault of the server; quote the request id when reporting it.

The server has more waiting work than it accepts: its queue of searches is full, the search would wait (or waited) longer for a worker than `queue_seconds` of /limits, or the server is stopping; the request was not searched. Retry after the `Retry-After` header's seconds, unchanged.

The request's search needed more time than its budget (`request_seconds` of /limits, counted from when its search began); `progress` says how far it went (identifiers of a batch, databases of each-database). The time a search takes depends on the server's load too, so the same request can succeed later; one refused again needs fewer identifiers or databases per request.

retry.title: Retry

source.title: Source

ErrorTerm.title: ErrorTerm
ErrorTerm.description: An error code of the api, its status and when it is answered.

nodes.title: Nodes

end.title: End

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: The inclusive release ranges at which the gene lies there.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: The region is part of the reference sequence (not a patch, a haplotype, an alternative locus or an LRG record).

release.title: Release

serving_assembly.title: Serving Assembly

external_databases.title: External Databases
external_databases.description: The external databases of the graph (any assembly), as `idtrack.API.external_databases` names them.

final_databases.title: Final Databases
final_databases.description: The databases a conversion to the snapshot release can end in.

from_release.title: From Release
from_release.description: The last release of the edges' earlier side.

to_release.title: To Release
to_release.description: The first release of the edges' later side.

version_changes.title: Version Changes
version_changes.description: Edges from a version of an id to another version of the same id.

id_changes.title: Id Changes
id_changes.description: Edges from a version of an id to a version of another id.

same_version.title: Same Version
same_version.description: Edges from a version to itself, with Ensembl's mapping score: the id and its version kept across a mapping session (the edge of an id alive at the graph's last release, which has no later side, is not counted).

retired.title: Retired
retired.description: Edges from a version to Ensembl's retirement marker of its id (`<id>.Retired`).

scored.title: Scored
scored.description: Of these edges, those with a mapping score of Ensembl's.

one_to_many.title: One To Many
one_to_many.description: Gene versions with history edges to two or more distinct gene versions across these releases (the version itself among them where it is kept; retirements not counted): the fan out of Ensembl's mapping, counted from the edges' ends, not idtrack's reading of a path's step (`split` of `PathStep.reason`). Sent by every answer of this version.

many_to_one.title: Many To One
many_to_one.description: Gene versions reached by history edges from two or more distinct gene versions across these releases: the fan in of Ensembl's mapping, counted the same way (not `merge` of `PathStep.reason`). Sent by every answer of this version.

HistoryTransition.title: HistoryTransition
HistoryTransition.description: The history edges between two releases: the last release of their earlier side and the first of their later.

method.title: Method
method.description: The HTTP method (a `GET` endpoint also takes `HEAD`).

path.title: Path

openapi.title: Openapi

llms_txt.title: Llms Txt
llms_txt.description: The index for language models (the llms.txt convention).

llms_full_txt.title: Llms Full Txt
llms_full_txt.description: Every rule, code and example of the api as one Markdown text.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: The reference for people, with a console per endpoint; `null` where no page is served.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.description: Every endpoint, in the document's order.

IndexResponse.title: IndexResponse
IndexResponse.description: Where everything is: the api's documents and every endpoint.

count.title: Count
count.description: The requests the percentiles are over.

most_recent.title: Most Recent
most_recent.description: The percentiles are over at most this many of the most recent requests...

window_seconds.title: Window Seconds
window_seconds.description: ...that ended within this many seconds before the sample.

p50_ms.title: P50 Ms
p50_ms.description: The median, in milliseconds (nearest rank); `null` with no request.

LatencyLoad.title: LatencyLoad
LatencyLoad.description: How long the server's recent requests took, from arrival to the last byte sent.

batch_max.title: Batch Max
batch_max.description: The most identifiers of one batch.

identifier_max_length.title: Identifier Max Length
identifier_max_length.description: The longest identifier or name, in characters.

body_max_bytes.title: Body Max Bytes
body_max_bytes.description: The largest request body, in bytes.

response_max_bytes.title: Response Max Bytes
response_max_bytes.description: The largest answer, in bytes; a larger one is refused, never cut.

request_seconds.title: Request Seconds
request_seconds.description: The time budget of one request's search, in seconds, from when its search begins (a batch: all its identifiers); a batch out of it is refused `503 request_budget_exceeded`, with the count it converted.

queue_seconds.title: Queue Seconds
queue_seconds.description: The longest a search waits for a worker free of searches, in seconds: a search still waiting then is answered `503 server_busy` without being searched, and one whose wait, estimated from the searches waiting before it and the recent searches' mean time, would pass it is answered so at once.

search_seconds.title: Search Seconds
search_seconds.description: The time budget of one identifier's search, in seconds.

search_states.title: Search States
search_states.description: The most search states one identifier's search may expand.

rate_per_minute.title: Rate Per Minute
rate_per_minute.description: Searching requests (conversions, batches, names) per minute per client; `0`: no per-client allowance of any kind. A client is its address, an IPv6 address by its `/64`. A searching request refused for what it holds before any search (a `4xx` other than `408`, `422` and `429`: a malformed or unknown argument, a batch over `batch_max`) is not counted here but among the reads.

rate_burst.title: Rate Burst
rate_burst.description: Searching requests a client may make at once before the rate applies.

read_share.title: Read Share
read_share.description: Every other request of the API (the tables and documents answered from memory, an answer sent again from the server's memory, a `304`) draws on an allowance this many times `rate_per_minute` and `rate_burst`; `/health` on none.

network_share.title: Network Share
network_share.description: The clients of one IPv6 `/48` network (65,536 `/64`) share, beside each one's own, allowances of searching requests and of reads this many times one client's; a `429` that one of them used up names the network in its message.

rate_search_seconds.title: Rate Search Seconds
rate_search_seconds.description: Seconds of search per minute per client: each search's own time (with writing and compressing its answer) is charged when its answer is written, and a client whose balance is below zero is answered `429` until it is back to zero; `0`: not limited.

rate_search_burst_seconds.title: Rate Search Burst Seconds
rate_search_burst_seconds.description: The most seconds of search a client's balance holds.

queue_max.title: Queue Max
queue_max.description: Searches that may wait for a worker, per worker: when every worker is in a search and `queue_max` times the workers wait, a search is answered `503 server_busy`.

head_seconds.title: Head Seconds
head_seconds.description: The longest a connection may take to send its request's head; it is closed after.

body_seconds.title: Body Seconds
body_seconds.description: The longest a request's body may take to arrive (`408 request_timeout` after).

answer_cache_bytes.title: Answer Cache Bytes
answer_cache_bytes.description: The answers each worker keeps to send again without a search (GETs, by `ETag`), in bytes; `0`: none.

allowances_enforced.title: Allowances Enforced
allowances_enforced.description: Whether the per-client allowances apply on this server (`rate_per_minute` above 0). When `false`, the bounds `allowance_fields` names are configured but not applied, and no answer is `429`; every other bound applies on every server.

allowance_fields.title: Allowance Fields
allowance_fields.description: The fields of this answer that are per-client allowances (applied only where `allowances_enforced` is `true`), in this answer's order; every other field is a bound of the server as a whole, always applied.

rate_concurrent_searches.title: Rate Concurrent Searches
rate_concurrent_searches.description: Searching requests a client may have in progress at once, from their admission until their answer is sent; more are answered `429` (`allowance` `concurrent_searches`) at once; `0`: not limited.

send_seconds.title: Send Seconds
send_seconds.description: The longest a client may leave an answer untaken (reading none of it) before its connection is closed.

send_min_bytes_per_second.title: Send Min Bytes Per Second
send_min_bytes_per_second.description: The slowest a client may take an answer, in bytes per second on average, once `send_seconds` have passed since its answer began; a slower client has its connection closed.

sending_max_bytes.title: Sending Max Bytes
sending_max_bytes.description: The most bytes of answers one worker holds for clients that have not taken them yet; an answer beyond is refused with `503 server_busy`.

LimitsResponse.title: LimitsResponse
LimitsResponse.description: The bounds this server enforces, as configured (SETUP.md, "Configuration").

content_digest.title: Content Digest
content_digest.description: The digest of the graph's content read.

releases.title: Releases

families.title: Families
families.description: The families of the graph: ids joined by history edges between two ids, through any number of others.

focus_families.title: Focus Families
focus_families.description: How many of the families given first hold a gene that the answers of the showcase name (`GET /organisms/{organism}/showcase`).

ids.title: Ids
ids.description: The gene ids given: whole families, first those that hold a gene the showcase's answers name (in the order they are named), then the others in the order of the SHA-256 digest of each family's smallest id, until the next family would pass `limit` (so every `limit` from one family's end to the next one's gives this same answer); within a family by the first release at which it is active, then by the id. Every other list of an id is in this order.

family_starts.title: Family Starts
family_starts.description: The index in `ids` of each family's first id, ascending.

active.title: Active
active.description: Per id, the runs of consecutive releases of the graph at which a version of it is active (idtrack's `TheGraph.active_releases`), each `[first, last]`.

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: Per id, the releases at which a history edge leads from one version of it to another, ascending.

edges.title: Edges
edges.description: History edges from a version of one id to a version of another, both given: `[from index, to index, old release, new release, score]`, `score` Ensembl's mapping score (the highest between the two ids across those releases) or `null` where it gave none. A version's edges to two or more ids at once is Ensembl's mapping fanning out, two or more ids' edges to one id fanning in; neither is idtrack's classification of a step of a path (`PathStep.reason`).

LineagesResponse.title: LineagesResponse
LineagesResponse.description: The lineages of gene ids of one graph as Ensembl's stable id history gives them, whole families at a time.

pss_bytes.title: Pss Bytes
pss_bytes.description: The sum of PSS over the master and the workers: the server's real footprint (each shared page counted once in all).

rss_bytes.title: Rss Bytes
rss_bytes.description: The sum of RSS over the processes: shared pages counted once per process, so more than the footprint when workers share the graphs.

uss_bytes.title: Uss Bytes
uss_bytes.description: The sum of USS: the pages that belong to one process alone.

limit_bytes.title: Limit Bytes
limit_bytes.description: The memory the server runs under: the smallest cgroup v2 `memory.max` of its cgroup and its ancestors (`source` `cgroup`), else the machine's total memory (`source` `meminfo`).

limit_used_bytes.title: Limit Used Bytes
limit_used_bytes.description: What is used of that limit: the limiting cgroup's `memory.current` (every process in it, page cache included), or the machine's total less its available memory.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the limit comes from; `null` when neither can be read.

MemoryLoad.title: MemoryLoad
MemoryLoad.description: The server's memory: its processes summed, and the limit it runs under.

match.description: How the identifier matched it (`match_steps` of `GET /vocabulary`, `match_prefixes` of `GET /vocabulary`).

x-match-prefixes.copy: In a batch: a name made unique by a single-cell tool (another item of the batch with -1, .1 or _1 appended, itself no exact name at the release it is read at alone); the result is that item's.
x-match-prefixes.unicode: Unicode was normalised before matching: invisible and control characters (zero-width characters, byte-order marks, bidirectional marks, soft hyphens) removed, compatibility forms (NFKC: full-width letters and digits) and Unicode dashes read as their plain characters.
x-match-prefixes.punctuation: Stray punctuation was removed before matching: quotes around the identifier, and the punctuation that ends a sentence, a clause or an item of a list at its end (a semicolon, comma, full stop, colon, exclamation or question mark).
x-match-prefixes.par_y: GENCODE's form of the Y copy of a pseudoautosomal gene (<id>_PAR_Y) was read as the gene's id; the Y copy is reported apart.
x-match-prefixes.lrg: An LRG record's id, answered with the gene the record describes.
x-match-prefixes.synonym: A synonym that a database records for the gene, not the name the database gives it.

x-match-steps.exact: The identifier as written (for an external identifier: as a database wrote it at the release read).
x-match-steps.case: The identifier when letter case is ignored.
x-match-steps.separator: The identifier when '-', '_' and '.' are taken as one character (and letter case is ignored).
x-match-steps.version: A sequence accession with the version written after it, read where Ensembl's cross references attached that version.
x-match-steps.version_newer_than_graph: An Ensembl id or a sequence accession with a version newer than every version the graph holds, read as its latest version (an id active, an accession attached, at the graph's last release).
x-match-steps.version_not_judged: A sequence accession with a version that is not judged: Ensembl's records hold only an edit counter of the records of its database (UniProt's entry version), so the accession is read without it.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it is reported: a key of `reading_reasons` of `GET /vocabulary`.
x-enum-descriptions: In an organism whose symbols follow a letter-case convention, a string written otherwise that is not exactly a name is read first as a symbol of the organism without letter case, where that names exactly one gene; this reading came after it.

The string ends in a suffix that single-cell tools append to make names unique (-1, .1, _1); reading it, with its separators taken as one or without letter case, as a synonym of another gene than the string before the suffix names is not taken.

The string means this identifier at other releases only (the releases listed), not at the release it was read at: what it meant at another time (a name of one gene then, a synonym of another gene now). Give from_release to read it there.

The string is an identifier followed by a version, and the identifier is, at the release read, also an id of a database that writes its ids without a version (an NCBI gene id spelt like a numeric Havana id of the early releases): where no database has the identifier with that version at that release, the string has two readings, and this is the other one (the identifier as that database's id, without the suffix).
The step that matched reached this identifier as well, at the same release; its candidates are part of the answer, ranked with those of the reading taken by the same evidence of lineage.

databases.description: For an external id, the databases that attach it to an Ensembl id at some release (for a synonym, the databases that record it); empty otherwise.

active.title: Active
active.description: For an Ensembl gene with version, the inclusive release ranges in which it exists (`null`: still active at the last release of the graph); empty otherwise.

assemblies.title: Assemblies
assemblies.description: For an Ensembl gene with version, the assemblies that serve its active releases.

non_reference.description: For an Ensembl gene, the release ranges in which it lies outside the reference sequence (an alternative locus, a patch, an LRG record).

places.title: Places

PathNode.title: PathNode
PathNode.description: A node of an explained path.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `identity` (the gene is its own answer), `entry` (from the identifier to the gene it stands for), `history` (an event of Ensembl's id history), `self_loop` (a scored re-mapping of a gene to itself), `bridge_near` and `bridge_far` (the two sides of a bridge through an id two genes carry), `final` (from the gene to its id in the final database).

source.title: Source
source.description: The node the step leaves (`null` for `identity`).

key.title: Key
key.description: The key of a history edge (Ensembl events between the same two ids); `null` otherwise.

release.title: Release
release.description: The release at which a cross-reference step holds (`null` for a final step of confidence 1, which holds at another release).

old_release.title: Old Release
old_release.description: For a history step: the old side of Ensembl's event, the last release of the event's earlier id. Ensembl's events run forward in time, the walk may not: walking forward the earlier id is `source`, walking backward (to an earlier target release) it is `target`.

new_release.title: New Release
new_release.description: For a history step: the new side of the event, the first release of the event's later id (`target` walking forward, `source` walking backward).

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: For a history step: Ensembl's mapping score (`null`: none given).

splits.title: Splits
splits.description: For a history step: the other ids that the event's earlier id passed to at `old_release` (a split), whatever the direction of the walk.

merges.title: Merges
merges.description: For a history step: the other ids that passed to the event's later id at `new_release` (a merge), whatever the direction of the walk.

databases.title: Databases
databases.description: For a cross-reference step: the databases that link the two nodes at the release on the assembly that serves it (for a synonym: the databases that record it).

assembly.title: Assembly
assembly.description: The assembly that serves `release` (or, for a history step, `new_release`, the event's new side).

old_assembly.title: Old Assembly
old_assembly.description: For a history step: the assembly that serves `old_release`, the event's old side (it differs from `assembly` where the event crosses from one assembly to the next); `null` otherwise.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the step was taken (or, for a step of `ExplainedPath.refused`, why it was not): a key of `step_reasons` of `GET /vocabulary`.
x-enum-descriptions: The gene exists at the target release.
The identifier is attached to this gene at the release it is read at.
Ensembl's id history: a new version of the id.
Ensembl's id history: the id was replaced by another.
Ensembl's id history: a split.
Ensembl's id history: a merge.
Ensembl's id history: a split and a merge.
Ensembl re-mapped the gene to itself with a score.
The history reaches no gene at the target release: the walk leaves the gene through an id it carries.
The walk enters another gene that carries the same id.
The gene carries the id in the final database at the target release.
The id is attached at the target release to a transcript or translation the gene had at another release.
Refused: Ensembl's history gives the id of a gene of the mitochondrial genome to a gene of a nuclear sequence, or the reverse; that is no lineage, and the walk does not follow it.
On one assembly the two genes overlap (one sequence region, one strand), or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies overlaps it.

On one assembly the two genes do not overlap: another sequence region, another strand, or apart; or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies shares no base with it; or a copy's reference region (Ensembl's assembly exception) shares no base with the other gene; or, on two assemblies that no published mapping joins, they lie on chromosomes of different names (the mitochondrial genome against a chromosome among them), which no assembly change turns one into the other.
The two genes never lie on one assembly at the same time, and nothing tells them apart (a sequence of one name, or a scaffold): their places cannot be compared.

A gene lies outside the reference sequence (a patch, a haplotype, an alternative locus, an LRG record), and nothing places it apart from the other gene (it lies inside its assembly exception's reference region, or it is an LRG record, which has none): its place is not compared base by base with the reference sequence.
The graph holds no place for one of the two genes.

places.title: Places
places.description: For a history step between two genes: where the event's later gene lies relative to the earlier one (a key of `place_relations` of `GET /vocabulary`; `places_apart`: Ensembl's history moves the gene to another place, which the walk follows); `null` for other steps.

PathStep.title: PathStep
PathStep.description: A step of an explained path.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When it began serving (UTC, ISO 8601): for the master, when the graphs were loaded; for a worker, its first request or sample after the fork.

cpu_share.title: Cpu Share
cpu_share.description: The share of one core it used over the last sampling interval: CPU time (user and system, all threads) over wall time between two samples; `1.0` is one core kept busy, and a process with several busy threads can exceed it. `null` until two samples exist, or where it cannot be measured.

cpu_seconds.title: Cpu Seconds
cpu_seconds.description: The CPU time it has used since it started, in seconds.

rss_bytes.title: Rss Bytes
rss_bytes.description: Resident set size: its pages in memory. A page the workers share with the master (the graphs, loaded before the fork) is counted in full in every process that maps it, so the RSS of the processes do not add up to the server's footprint.

pss_bytes.title: Pss Bytes
pss_bytes.description: Proportional set size: its resident pages, each shared page divided by the number of processes sharing it. The sum over the server's processes is the server's real footprint.

uss_bytes.title: Uss Bytes
uss_bytes.description: Unique set size: its pages no other process maps (what it would free on exit).

cpu_sample_age_seconds.title: Cpu Sample Age Seconds
cpu_sample_age_seconds.description: Seconds between its last sample of CPU and this answer; `null` if it was never sampled.

memory_sample_age_seconds.title: Memory Sample Age Seconds
memory_sample_age_seconds.description: Seconds between its last sample of memory and this answer; `null` if it was never sampled.

ProcessLoad.title: ProcessLoad
ProcessLoad.description: One process of the server (the master, or a worker): its CPU and memory as last sampled.

answered.title: Answered
answered.description: The items answered within the budget.

of.title: Of
of.description: The items the request asked for.

items.title: Items
items.description: What was counted: the distinct identifiers of a batch, or the databases of `GET .../convert/each-database`.

Progress.title: Progress
Progress.description: How far a request's search went before its time budget ran out.

total.title: Total
total.description: Requests answered since the server started, by every worker, replaced ones included.

in_flight.title: In Flight
in_flight.description: Requests held now by the live workers.

searches_running.title: Searches Running
searches_running.description: Searches running now (at most one per worker).

searches_waiting.title: Searches Waiting
searches_waiting.description: Searches a worker holds that wait for its own search thread (behind the search it runs). The three counts of waiting requests (this, `searches_queued` and `connections_waiting`) never hold the same request twice: their sum is every request waiting.

connections_waiting.title: Connections Waiting
connections_waiting.description: Connections in the kernel's listen queue that no worker has taken yet (the kernel's count); `null`: not read, as when the app runs without the server.

searches_queued.title: Searches Queued
searches_queued.description: Searches waiting in the queue the workers share for a worker free of searches (every worker is in one); `null` when the app runs without the server.

sending_bytes.title: Sending Bytes
sending_bytes.description: Bytes of answers the live workers hold for clients that have not taken them yet (bounded per worker by `sending_max_bytes` of `GET /limits`).

last_60_seconds.title: Last 60 Seconds
last_60_seconds.description: Requests answered in the last 60 seconds (counted per whole second).

errors_4xx.title: Errors 4Xx
errors_4xx.description: Requests answered with a status of 400 to 499 since the server started.

errors_5xx.title: Errors 5Xx
errors_5xx.description: Requests answered with a status of 500 or more since the server started.

lost.title: Lost
lost.description: Requests a worker held when it ended without giving back its row (killed by the master's timeout, the kernel's out-of-memory killer or a signal): their clients got no answer.

status_requests.title: Status Requests
status_requests.description: Requests to `/status` since the server started (counted apart from every count above).

latency.description: The latency of the server's most recent requests (`/status` not counted), in milliseconds.

RequestsLoad.title: RequestsLoad
RequestsLoad.description: The server's requests, over every worker (requests to `/status` are counted apart, in `status_requests`).

result.description: The answer, exactly as `GET .../convert` gives it; `null` when the request was refused.

error.description: The refusal (as `GET .../convert` would answer it), with `request_id` `showcase`; else `null`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The phenomenon its answer shows, read from the answer's own fields: `new_version`, `replaced`, `merge` or `final` (the best candidate's path takes a step of that reason), `renamed` (a step `final`, the identifier read in the database it is answered in, and no best target the identifier itself), `split` (a step `split` or `split_and_merge`), `handoff` (a history step between two assemblies), `bridge` (steps `bridge_near` and `bridge_far`), `other_release` (an other reading of reason `other_release`), `tie` (status `tie`), `retired` (status `no_conversion` with the reason `no_path_to_target`), `refused` (a refused step of reason `mitochondrial_genome` in `path.refused`), `lineage` (the best candidate's path holds steps on every assembly of the graph).

ShowcaseCase.title: ShowcaseCase
ShowcaseCase.description: A chosen conversion that shows one phenomenon of Ensembl's history.

result.description: The answer, exactly as `GET .../convert` gives it; `null` when the request was refused.

error.description: The refusal (as `GET .../convert` would answer it), with `request_id` `showcase`; else `null`.

ShowcaseItem.title: ShowcaseItem
ShowcaseItem.description: A chosen conversion and its answer.

content_digest.description: The digest of the graph's content.

cases.title: Cases
cases.description: The cases' queries and kinds, in order.

ShowcaseQueriesResponse.title: ShowcaseQueriesResponse
